question: In Figure 8 (Page 12), how does the calibration curve and Expected Calibration Error (ECE) on MMLU change between the pre-trained GPT-4 model (Left) and the post-trained PPO GPT-4 model (Right)?
expected_answer: In Figure 8 (Page 12), the pre-trained GPT-4 model (Left) is well-calibrated along the diagonal with an ECE of 0.007, whereas the post-trained PPO GPT-4 model (Right) has significantly worse calibration (overconfident, falling below the diagonal) with an ECE of 0.074.

gold.evidence: Left plot: Calibration curve (model=pre-train) ... ECE = 0.007. Right plot: Calibration curve (model=ppo) ... ECE = 0.074.

answer: In Figure 8, the calibration on a subset of the MMLU dataset changes significantly between the pre-trained and post-trained models. The pre-trained GPT-4 model (Left) closely tracks the diagonal line representing perfect calibration, with an Expected Calibration Error (ECE) of 0.007 [gpt4-2023-techreport_p012_chart_01]. In contrast, the post-trained PPO (RLHF) GPT-4 model (Right) is significantly overconfident, with its calibration curve falling well below the diagonal line, resulting in an ECE of 0.074, which is over 10x worse than the pre-trained model [gpt4-2023-tech-report_p012_chart_01]. The text confirms that post-training hurts calibration significantly [gpt4-2023-tech-report_p012_text_01].

[IMAGE_DIAGRAM: Table 17 | Page 37 | BBox (55, 55, 555, 720)]
- Visual Input Example (Table 17 — Pixel to Paper Summaries): Three page-screenshot images of the InstructGPT paper (including Figure 2 architecture diagram of the 3-step RLHF pipeline).
- User follow-up prompt on diagram: 'Could you explain the process described in Figure 2?'
- Three steps read from Figure 2 diagram in the screenshot:
  1. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT): Collect labeler demonstration data of prompts and desired output behavior to fine-tune GPT-3.
  2. Reward model (RM) training: Collect human labeler rankings of several model outputs from best to worst to train the reward model.
  3. Reinforcement learning using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO): Optimize the SFT policy against the reward model using PPO.

We report the development of GPT-4, a large-scale, multimodal model which can accept image and text inputs and produce text outputs. While less capable than humans in many real-world scenarios, GPT-4 exhibits human-level performance on various professional and academic benchmarks, including passing a simulated bar exam with a score around the top 10% of test takers. GPT-4 is a Transformer- based model pre-trained to predict the next token in a document. The post-training alignment process results in improved performance on measures of factuality and adherence to desired behavior. A core component of this project was developing infrastructure and optimization methods that behave predictably across a wide range of scales. This allowed us to accurately predict some aspects of GPT-4’s performance based on models trained with no more than 1/1,000th the compute of GPT-4.

3For AMC 10 and AMC 12 2022 exams, the human percentiles are not yet published, so the reported numbers are extrapolated and likely have wide uncertainty. See Appendix A.5. 4We used the post-trained RLHF model for these exams.

This report focuses on the capabilities, limitations, and safety properties of GPT-4. GPT-4 is a Transformer-style model [39] pre-trained to predict the next token in a document, using both publicly available data (such as internet data) and data licensed from third-party providers. The model was then fine-tuned using Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) [40]. Given both the competitive landscape and the safety implications of large-scale models like GPT-4, this report contains no further details about the architecture (including model size), hardware, training compute, dataset construction, training method, or similar.
